text.p: By Alex Gosman (executive director of Australian Telecommunications Industry Association, ATIA)
The Australian telecommunications equipment industry has been one of the "quiet achievers" associated with the reforms to the Australian telecommunications environment over the past five years.

Under a favourable policy environment that has encouraged close links between industry and the carriers in the deregulating environment, exports by the Australian telecommunications industry have been one of the drivers of the big increase in exports of Australian manufactures in the past decade.
In 1995 exports of telecommunications equipment accounted for A$1.0 billion - nearly six percent of all exports of elaborately transformed manufactures (ETM).
ETM exports have increased from A$190 million in 1989/90.
At the same time domestic production has increased and in 1995 reached A$4.5 billion, with R&D of nearly A$300 million - the highest as a percentage of turnover of any industry sector.

The extent of policy considerations associated with the telecommunications industry in Australia continues to grow apace as does the requirement upon industry to participate in a range of deliberations and provide comment and input.
Over the next six months the following issues are of the highest priority for the telecommunications equipment industry.
- continuing input into the post 1997 regulatory arrangements for the telecommunications industry in such areas as industry development, technical regulation, access arrangements.

- involvement into the recently initiated IT&T (Informational Technology and Telecommunications) Competitiveness Study and the Information Industries Taskforce which will examine prospects for the IT&T industries and the effectiveness of existing industry support programs such as Partnership for Developement.

- responding to the changes of a number of industry programmes and delivery mechanisms arising from the recent Budget (such as the changes to AUSTRADE and its re-organisation) and briefing members on the implications.

- continuing involvement in changes to spectrum policy including spectrum licensing, band clearance. With the growth in wireless applications, policies on the allocation of spectrum and its pricing will have significant implications for the take-up of this new technology.
Many of the above issues are interconnected and are vital to the continuing growth of the industry.

Recently the ATIA has commented favourably upon the first tranche of draft legislation issued by the Department of Communications and the Arts covering proposals in respect of industry development commitments and future technical regulation.

In addition to the above priorities there are ongoing tasks such as involvement in a number of forthcoming trade missions, preparation of capability brochures, government purchasing reforms etc. In mid-September the ATIA also meet with the minister for science and technology, Peter McGauran to discuss standards related issues impacting on future telecommunications arrangements, particularly the accreditation of standards writing bodies.
(Views are those of the author, not those of Reuters)
